types.name: K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization)
types.purpose: Online pre-travel authorisation for short stays (tourism, visiting relatives, events, meetings, non-profit business) without a visa.
types.who: Nationals of visa-free countries that are not exempt
types.maxValidity: 3 years, or until passport expiry if sooner
types.note: Usually 90 days per stay but depends on nationality (some 30 days). Several nationalities are temporarily exempt; check the current list. Not a visa; entry decided at the border.

types.name: Short-term visit, general tourist (C-3-9)
types.purpose: Tourism, visiting relatives or recuperation for up to 90 days, for nationalities that need a visa.
types.note: Some nationalities are granted a shorter stay (e.g. 30 days).

types.name: Short-term visit for events or meetings (C-3-1)
types.purpose: Short stay to attend events or meetings, perform cultural arts, take lessons or training, or similar.
types.who: Visitors with an event, meeting or short course

types.name: Short-term business visitor (C-3-4)
types.purpose: Business meetings, market research, liaison work, consultations or contract signing.
types.note: Multiple entry only if the Korean inviting company requests it with a reason.

types.name: Visa-free transit tourism (B-2)
types.purpose: Visa-free entry for passengers travelling through Korea to a third country with an onward ticket.
types.who: Eligible nationalities holding a valid visa or residence for certain countries
types.note: Third-country program: up to 30 days with a flight out within 30 days. Separate Incheon transit tour: connecting flight within 72 hours. Some nationalities excluded; the consulate cannot confirm eligibility.

types.name: Visa-free entry to Jeju Island
types.purpose: Visa-free entry for visa-required nationals arriving on a direct flight to Jeju.
types.note: Stay length not stated on the official page found; call the Immigration Call Center (+82-2-6908-1345). Applies to direct flights to Jeju only.

types.name: Workation / digital nomad (F-1-D)
types.purpose: Remote work for a foreign employer or own foreign company while living in Korea.
types.who: Remote workers with foreign employment of 1+ year and sufficient income
types.maxValidity: 1 year, multiple entry; extendable up to 1 year
types.note: No work for Korean employers or profit-making work in Korea. Income at least twice previous-year GNI per capita.

types.name: Student, degree study (D-2)
types.purpose: Study for a degree, research or exchange at a Korean university.
types.who: Students admitted to a Korean university
types.maxValidity: Initial stay up to 2 years, per Certificate of Admission; visa typically single entry valid 3 months
types.note: Foreigner registration within 90 days if staying over 91 days; multiple entry possible afterwards.

types.name: Visiting student, under 1 year (D-2-8)
types.purpose: Study at a Korean university for up to one year while enrolled at an overseas university.
types.who: Overseas degree students on exchange or self-funded
types.maxValidity: Up to 12 months, per Certificate of Admission
types.note: Required even for summer or winter programmes under 90 days if credits are earned.

types.name: Job seeker (D-10-1)
types.purpose: Seeking employment or training in fields eligible for E-1 to E-7 visas.
types.who: Points-qualified graduates or ex-employees of listed firms
types.note: Stay of 6 months or less; needs at least 60 points.

types.name: Working Holiday (H-1)
types.purpose: Travel with incidental work under a bilateral working holiday agreement.
types.maxValidity: Varies by country (e.g. up to 18 months for US citizens)
types.note: US: ages 18-30, quota 2,000, enter within 12 months of issue. No professional jobs; language teaching needs E-2. Terms vary by country.

types.name: Professor (E-1)
types.purpose: Lecturing or research at a college or university.

types.name: Foreign language instructor (E-2)
types.purpose: Teaching foreign language conversation at schools or institutes.

types.name: Specially designated activities (E-7)
types.purpose: Work in occupations designated by the Minister of Justice for a Korean employer.
types.who: Professionals and skilled workers with a contract
types.note: Usually needs a Certificate of Visa Issuance Confirmation from Korean immigration first.

types.name: Non-professional employment (E-9)
types.purpose: Unskilled work in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, fishing and services under the Employment Permit System.

types.name: Marriage migrant (F-6)
types.purpose: Living in Korea as spouse of a Korean national, or as parent raising a Korean citizen's child.
types.who: Spouses and parents of Korean nationals
types.maxValidity: Consulate visa single entry up to 90 days; stay 3 years once extended in Korea

types.name: Resident (F-2)
types.purpose: Long-term residence, e.g. for family of Korean or permanent-resident nationals, recognised refugees, and points-based residents.

types.name: Overseas Korean (F-4)
types.purpose: Residence for people of Korean heritage with foreign nationality.
types.note: Employment restricted for simple labour and some workplaces.

types.name: Permanent resident (F-5)
types.purpose: Permanent residence with no restrictions on activities, including employment.
types.who: Long-term residents, e.g. 5+ years in F-2
types.note: Re-entry permit exemption: 2 years for F-5 holders.
